beats.text: The pattern shows that in the data there is a commonality of what was dropped. This is curious as we would expect an increase in 'meta' and a decrease in unknown to mean that there was a rise in well-categorized news articles. However, none of these summaries can show us what topics were being well categorized because the key details about the stories are being omitted, and only trends are being highlighted. <think> </think> The AI model data is incomplete — it tells us there was an increase in meta and a decrease in unknown but doesn't tell us how. The model summarizes without providing specific information on what was summarized. There is a gap between what the summaries state they have done, and what information we are given. We don't know exactly what topics or subjects were being well-categorized. This isn't simply about omissions — it's that in all three cases, there is no indication of any actual content. It seems like something is going wrong with this summarization process. Is the AI summarizing the wrong data? Or are we not getting a true reflection of what was actually happening? If these summaries are accurate, then this shows us that the model can only summarize trends and cannot identify specific events or subjects.
